result.title: Preface
result.summary: The March 2021 San Bernardino County Employees’ Retirement Association RFP seeks investment consulting services. Its contents cover the introduction, background, timeline, services, minimum qualifications, public-contracting ethics, proposal submission requirements, official notices and addenda, applicable law, and the investment consulting agreement. Proposals must include a cover letter, table of contents, executive summary, questionnaire, fee schedule, references, and additional information. The questionnaire addresses the firm’s background and organization, staff, qualifications, advised assets, consulting philosophy and process, manager measurement and evaluation, manager searches and evaluation, and miscellaneous matters. The RFP also describes overall scoring criteria, the recommendation process, and notice to proposers concerning the California Public Records Act, and includes a sample investment consulting services agreement.

result.title: Request for Proposals for Investment Consulting Services
result.summary: SBCERA’s March 1, 2021 RFP seeks a qualified firm for full-retainer, comprehensive pension investment consulting covering the entire portfolio, including general advice and private equity, private credit, real estate, real assets, and absolute-return/hedge funds. Questions were due by email to the RFP Administrator, Donald Pierce, CIO, on March 16 at 4 p.m. PDT; answers were to be posted March 23. Proposals were due by email only on April 16 at 4 p.m. PDT. Respondents must not contact staff or trustees directly; staff may request clarification. Established in 1945 under CERL, SBCERA is a California cost-sharing defined-benefit plan serving nearly 42,000 members and beneficiaries across 17 employers. Its nine-member Board and three alternates oversee a roughly $12 billion globally diversified portfolio, managed by the CIO under Board policies, with external fund and direct investments, master-account arrangements, and an overlay manager for informed rebalancing. The timeline also lists an Investment Committee meeting July 13 and a Board contract-approval meeting August 5, if needed.

result.title: IV. Services Provided
result.summary: SBCERA seeks an investment consultant for up to seven years to advise on its entire portfolio, report to the Board through staff, and act as an unqualified fiduciary solely in participants’ and beneficiaries’ interests, following the Plan’s investment guidelines. Duties include developing and monitoring investment policies; annual asset-allocation reviews and portfolio-structure advice; assessing managers, conducting searches, selections, terminations and due diligence, advising on traditional and alternative investments, and ongoing manager monitoring. The consultant will review manager and portfolio risk and performance, provide quarterly analyses by fund, asset class and manager against policy benchmarks and peer groups, and offer analytical software access if available. Client services include weekly staff meetings, Board and committee attendance, ad hoc workshops, research, requested education and presentations at the annual Investment Forum, and regular operational communication. The consultant will also coordinate with the actuarial and operational due-diligence consultants and custodian bank.

result.title: Consultant Qualifications and Public Contracting Ethics
result.summary: SBCERA accepts proposals only from firms meeting all minimum qualifications by December 31, 2020: registration as an investment adviser under the Investment Company Act of 1940; at least seven years in business; three or more U.S. public pension clients, each with at least $5 billion in assets; no material litigation, claims, SEC censure, or regulatory action in the prior seven years; a proposed lead consultant with at least ten years’ public defined-benefit pension consulting experience; and proof of at least $10 million in professional liability coverage per occurrence and/or aggregate. By responding, proposers certify their proposals are free of collusion and fraud, disclaim kickbacks or inducements, and attest they have not provided anything of value to public employees to secure the contract. They also agree not to have substantively interacted with procurement officials—including SBCERA legal or investment staff, executive management, or Board members—except as and when the RFP allows.

result.title: VII. Submission of Proposals
result.summary: Submit proposals electronically to the RFP Administrator by the stated deadline, using the specified email subject. SBCERA may interview qualified proposers and invite finalists to present to the Board. Responses must have numbered pages in 8½-by-11-inch format and include, in order, a cover letter, contents, executive summary (maximum three pages), completed questionnaire, fee schedule, and references; additional information may be appended. The signed, authorized cover letter must identify enclosures and include completeness/minimum-qualification assurances; proposer and contact details, tax ID, a 240-day irrevocable offer, service commitment, regulatory/legal and nondiscrimination certifications, confidentiality designations, genuine pricing/no-collusion and no-inducement certifications, conflict disclosure, five-year relationships with SBCERA personnel, and fiduciary acknowledgment. Use a numbered table of contents; answer questionnaire items in order, reproducing each question. Itemize general and alternative consulting retainer fees, include all costs, and guarantee fees for seven years; escalation may be proposed, but final fees cannot exceed quoted fees. Provide at least three references (two familiar with proposed team members) and list pension clients ending service within five years, with size, termination date, and reasons.

result.title: VIII. Official RFP Notices/ Addenda
result.summary:
VIII. Official RFP Notices/ Addenda
To ensure that no firm is provided an advantage over another, all requirements are specified in this Request for Proposals (RFP). Any changes to the requirements will be posted as an addendum to the RFP on the SBCERA website. Firms are solely responsible for monitoring the website for and adhering to any RFP addenda. SBCERA reserves the right to withdraw this RFP at any time without prior notice and to reject any and all responses to this RFP. The rejection of any or all RFP shall not render SBCERA liable for costs or damages.

result.title: IX. Applicable Law
result.summary:
IX. Applicable Law
This solicitation and any resulting contract shall be governed, in all respects, by the laws of the State of California, and any litigation with respect thereto shall be brought in the Superior Court of San Bernardino County, California, and shall not be brought in, nor subject to removal to, any other court. The Proposer shall comply with all applicable federal, state and local laws, rules and regulations.
All Proposers must acknowledge and agree to be a fiduciary to SBCERA with the same prudence as imposed upon SBCERA pursuant to Section 31595 of the 1937 Act in the performance of all services rendered pursuant to any contract resulting from this RFP process.

result.title: X. Questionnaire
result.summary: The questionnaire requests, in order: proposer contact details and firm background, structure, ownership, finances, staffing, experience, regulatory or legal history, and growth, capacity, and acquisition plans; staffing model, outsourced services, key personnel’s roles, qualifications, experience, resumes, disciplinary history, compensation, retention incentives, and links between client satisfaction and staff performance; qualifications, comparable public-pension clients, experience with master custody account arrangements, and ability to meet SBCERA’s needs; 2018–2020 full-service client, advised-asset, and renewal figures, plus client gains and losses and termination reasons; consulting philosophy, asset-allocation review practices and sample, allocation ranges, liquidity recommendations, risk methods and metrics, and performance measurement; investment-performance monitoring, databases, benchmarks, reporting timelines and samples, custodian data validation, and return reconciliation; manager research, database and rating processes, strategies assessed, and sample due-diligence reports; and conflicts and mitigation, client relationship and resource allocation, insurance limits and terms, and other relevant information.

result.title: XI. Investment Consulting Agreement
result.summary: Proposals are binding offers, and the winning contract will incorporate the RFP, draft contract, and proposal without deviation; it may not be assigned. The anticipated term is January 1, 2022–January 1, 2027, with a Board option to extend through January 1, 2029, and termination on 30 days’ notice with or without cause. Proposals will be evaluated for quality, relevant firm experience, assigned personnel, scope and service model, and fee value, including qualitative cost considerations. Recommendations were scheduled for the July 13, 2021 Investment Committee meeting and, if needed, the August 5 Board meeting. Under California public-records law, proposals become public when a recommendation appears on a public agenda. Legally exempt trade secrets must be conspicuously marked in red; marking an entire proposal confidential is invalid. SBCERA is not liable for legally required disclosure, and proposers must indemnify it for certain attorney fees resulting from refusal to disclose marked material. Submission waives claims concerning privacy, trade-secret disclosure, or inspection-related damage.

result.title: Contract Terms, Proposal Scoring, and Recommendation
result.summary: The contract will incorporate the RFP, attached draft contract, and winning proposal without deviation, and cannot be assigned. The anticipated term is January 1, 2022, through January 1, 2027, with a possible Board-approved two-year extension through January 1, 2029. The Board may terminate with or without cause on 30 days’ notice. Proposals will be scored on proposal quality; relevant firm experience; assigned personnel’s quality and experience; scope and service-delivery model; and fee value, assessed qualitatively as well as by cost. A recommendation based on RFP responses will go to the SBCERA Investment Committee on July 13, 2021, and, if necessary, staff and committee recommendations will proceed to the full Board on August 5, 2021.

result.title: XIV. Notice to Proposers regarding the California Publics Records Act
result.summary: The notice explains that the California Public Records Act grants public access to records of government business. RFP responses become SBCERA property and, once an evaluation recommendation is placed on a public agenda, are public records available upon request, except legally protected trade secrets or confidential business information conspicuously marked in red ink. SBCERA is not liable for disclosures required by law or court order; proposers must indemnify it for attorney fees awarded because it refused to disclose marked material. Proposals cannot be designated entirely confidential; doing so is invalid and makes the entire proposal public. Submission waives claims against SBCERA and its representatives concerning privacy violations, disclosure of trade secrets, or resulting damages. The text also introduces Exhibit A, a template investment consulting services agreement between SBCERA and a blank consultant.

result.title: INVESTMENT CONSULTANT AGREEMENT
result.summary: The agreement, effective on a date to be specified and made in San Bernardino, California, is between the San Bernardino County Employees’ Retirement Association (SBCERA) and a consultant. It recites that SBCERA was established under the County Employees Retirement Law of 1937 and is administered by its Board of Retirement, which may invest or delegate investment authority under the prudent-person standard in Government Code Section 31595. The consultant represents that it qualifies as an ERISA fiduciary, is registered under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, has relevant experience, and will provide the specified investment consulting services as an SBCERA fiduciary. The Board has determined that retaining the consultant for services concerning the Fund is in SBCERA’s best interest and approved the agreement. The consultant warrants its willingness and ability to perform, acknowledges SBCERA is a governmental employee benefits plan administered in San Bernardino County, and is retained under the agreement’s terms. The recitals are incorporated into the agreement.

result.title: ARTICLE 1 DESCRIPTION OF INVESTMENT CONSULTING SERVICES
key_items: 1.4 Seminars and Training Programs. In the event CONSULTANT conducts seminars, training sessions or similar events which are generally made available to CONSULTANT's
result.summary: The Board delegates the investment consulting services in Exhibit A to the Consultant, which accepts them subject to the agreement and applicable law. The Board retains all investment decision-making authority; the Consultant has no discretion over or custody of plan assets, and the Board relies on its advice. The Consultant and its service providers must meet California and Advisers Act fiduciary standards, including prudence, loyalty, and timely disclosure of potential conflicts; prior conflicts are represented as disclosed. The Consultant is liable for claims arising from fiduciary failures. Its engagement is nonexclusive, and additional services are unpaid unless authorized in writing with separate compensation or reimbursement. The Consultant must monitor and advise on Investment Plan amendments and comply with the existing plan until amendments are approved, then follow the amended plan. SBCERA may attend generally offered seminars on the same terms as other customers; if the Consultant reimburses customers’ event or travel costs, it must reimburse SBCERA on the same basis, but not individual attendees.

result.title: ARTICLE 2 CONTRACT RESPONSIBILITIES
result.summary: Article 2 defines both parties’ representative responsibilities. SBCERA’s CEO or designee administers the Agreement, directs policy and procedures, receives regular service reports, and may issue binding written directions or interpretations, but cannot amend or otherwise bind SBCERA; Board-reserved approvals remain with the Board, and reviews do not relieve the Consultant of responsibility. The Consultant should allow 15 business days for responses, share information only with designated contacts, and submit supported invoices no more than quarterly; expense and third-party charges are due within 60 days. Payment is generally reviewed and made within 30 days, subject to Exhibit C, and SBCERA staff have no personal official-capacity liability. The Consultant’s full-time Senior Consultant handles day-to-day services and communications; alternate or replacement appointments require specified Board consent or approval, and the Board may require ineffective staff to be replaced. The Consultant retains supervision, must promptly report staffing changes, and needs prior approval for agents or sub-advisors while remaining liable for them and applying the Fiduciary Standard. The Consultant and Fund must avoid prohibited counterparties and comply with applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and anti-money-laundering laws.

nodes.title: 2.1 SBCERA – REPRESENTATIVE RESPONSIBILITIES.
key_items: 2.1.1 Representative. The SBCERA's representative for this Agreement will be:
nodes.summary: SBCERA’s representative is CEO Deborah S. Cherney (San Bernardino County Employees’ Retirement Association, 348 West Hospitality Lane, Suite 100, San Bernardino, CA 92408; (909) 885-7980; fax (909) 885-7446), or her designee. The representative administers the Agreement; the Consultant must regularly report on service status, cooperate with delegated personnel, and accept written notice of changes to the representative or notice address. The representative directs policy, information, and procedures. Written directions and interpretations may bind SBCERA, except approvals reserved to the Board; reviews do not lessen the Consultant’s responsibility for meeting the Agreement. The representative cannot amend the Agreement or otherwise bind SBCERA, and the Consultant should allow 15 business days for responses. Invoices require supporting documents and approval, may be submitted no more than quarterly, and expense/third-party charges must be submitted within 60 days; submission certifies amounts are due and reimbursed items were received, satisfactory, and benefited SBCERA. Review and payment are generally due within 30 days, subject to Exhibit C limits. The Consultant may share information only with designated SBCERA contacts. SBCERA personnel have no personal liability for actions or omissions in their official roles.

nodes.title: 2.2 CONSULTANT – REPRESENTATIVE RESPONSIBILITIES.
key_items: 2.2.1 Representative. The CONSULTANT's representatives for this Agreement
2.2.2 Authority of Senior Consultant. The Senior Consultant is fully authorized to act on behalf of and to receive communications on the part of CONSULTANT.
nodes.summary: The agreement identifies a full-time Senior Consultant responsible for day-to-day services and administration, regular reporting to SBCERA, and receiving communications and acting for the Consultant. A Senior Alternate requires Board written consent. Board approval is generally required to replace either senior representative, subject to a reasonableness limit when affiliation ends; the Consultant must promptly report proposed replacements and known termination or replacement requests. The Board may require replacement of ineffective personnel, while the Consultant retains supervision and direction. Agents or sub-advisors require prior written approval from the SBCERA Investment Officer; the Consultant remains liable for their conduct and must select them consistently with the Fiduciary Standard. The Consultant and Fund may not knowingly transact with sanctioned or otherwise prohibited persons, known entities they own or control, or persons based or principally operating in restricted countries. Counterparty representations may satisfy reasonable inquiry. Payments must comply with U.S. and U.K. anti-bribery laws and applicable anti-corruption and anti-money-laundering rules. “Person” includes governments, territories, and political entities.

result.title: ARTICLE 3 PAYMENT FOR SERVICES
result.summary: The consultant’s fees are set out in Exhibit C and paid upon invoices submitted under Subsection 2.1.3. Payment is quarterly in arrears for services performed in the preceding calendar quarter, prorated by days worked. The fee schedule applies from a specified date in 2022 through a specified date in 2027 and may be extended to 2029 under Section 7.1. Upon renewal, the parties may renegotiate fees effective on or after a specified date; any new schedule must be mutually agreed in a written amendment. These fees are the sole compensation owed by or to any person for the consultant’s services.

result.title: ARTICLE 4 CONSULTANT'S REPRESENTATIONS, WARRANTIES, COVENANTS AND CERTIFICATIONS
key_items: 4.1 CONSULTANT's Representations, Warranties and Covenants. CONSULTANT acknowledges, represents, warrants, and agrees that:
result.summary: The consultant represents and covenants that it is qualified as an ERISA investment consultant and fiduciary, will maintain that status, act solely in SBCERA’s interests under prudent-care and applicable California standards, and is not ERISA-disqualified. It confirms required regulatory compliance, experienced personnel without specified misconduct, active investment-adviser registration, and acceptance of fiduciary duties without relying on SBCERA or County officials for advice. It confirms timely delivery of its SEC Form ADV, no specified regulatory complaints or disciplinary actions in the prior 24 months, and that its proposal is materially accurate. These assurances are material inducements to the agreement. The consultant warrants and agrees not to offer gratuities to influence the award or administration of the agreement and will review applicable conflict-of-interest laws. It represents that relevant SBCERA employees, fiduciaries, spouses, and dependents have no employment or financial interests in the consultant or agreement, and will provide annual or requested certifications. It also warrants that no contingent-fee solicitation arrangement was used, except for bona fide employees or established sales agencies.

result.title: ARTICLE 5 CONFLICTS OF INTEREST AND PERMITTED DEALINGS
result.summary: The consultant represents that no compensation has been paid to placement agents or to SBCERA-related personnel to secure the agreement, access, or favorable advice, and agrees to comply with SBCERA’s placement-agent, gifts, and campaign-contributions policy; violations may result in termination. The consultant may serve other clients if doing so does not violate or adversely affect its fiduciary duties to SBCERA. Before recommending any person, contract, or transaction involving a financial or economic interest of the consultant, specified personnel, their affiliates or associates, or, to their knowledge, their clients, the consultant must disclose the interest fully in writing and certify it will not affect the recommendation.

result.title: ARTICLE 6 CONSULTANT DISCLOSURES
key_items: 6.1 Changes in Ownership. The CONSULTANT will promptly contact and provide a written statement to the Board: whenever there are material adverse changes in its
result.summary: The consultant must promptly notify the Board in writing of material adverse financial changes or significant business changes, including ownership changes of 25% or more and key personnel changes; material litigation or regulatory proceedings that could affect the Accounts or Portfolio; and any agreement representations, certifications, acknowledgements, or warranties that cease to be true (notifying SBCERA). It must provide its policies on handling material non-public information and on managing and disclosing conflicts of interest, and annually reaffirm its conflict policies and provide amendments. It must also promptly report in writing to the Board Chair and/or SBCERA Investment Officer any non-routine contact by specified SBCERA or County of San Bernardino representatives advocating or requesting a particular contract, investment professional, investment, trade, strategy, product, or related inclusion or exclusion.

result.title: ARTICLE 7 TERM AND TERMINATION
key_items: 7.2.4 CONSULTANT will cooperate with the SBCERA in effecting a smooth transition to a new consultant after any termination hereunder.
result.summary: The Agreement runs for five years from the specified 2022 start date through the specified 2027 end date, with the Board’s option to extend it for two years through a specified 2029 date. Either party may terminate for any reason by written notice effective at least 30 days later; obligations continue during the notice period unless SBCERA suspends services. After notice, SBCERA may immediately suspend some or all of the Consultant’s authority, including its ability to make commitments binding SBCERA, while remaining liable for fees earned through termination. Termination does not waive claims under Section 8.2, and Section 7 remedies supplement other available remedies. The Consultant must assist with transition to a replacement and, within 30 calendar days after expiration or termination, deliver to the Board all previously undelivered records and work-product information, subject to Advisers Act recordkeeping requirements.

result.title: ARTICLE 8 INSURANCE AND INDEMNIFICATION
result.summary: The Consultant must maintain required insurance throughout the Agreement for claims arising from its work, provide evidence before work begins, and give SBCERA’s requested policy documents; SBCERA may review coverage and require a meeting if protection is inadequate. Coverage includes commercial general liability naming SBCERA as additional insured and primary ($1 million per occurrence/$5 million aggregate), statutory workers’ compensation, professional liability ($5 million per occurrence and aggregate), fidelity coverage ($10 million per occurrence and aggregate), and cyber coverage ($10 million aggregate). SBCERA must approve deductibles and self-insured retentions, which may require reduction or security. Claims-made professional liability must have an appropriate retroactive date and, if not replaced, at least five years’ extended reporting coverage; insurers must meet specified financial ratings or receive approval. General liability policies must waive subrogation against SBCERA and related personnel. The Consultant must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless SBCERA and its related personnel for service-related claims and costs, subject to reimbursement if a court finds indemnification unavailable. The section sets claim-notice, defense, counsel-conflict, participation, and settlement-consent rules.

nodes.title: ARTICLE 8 INSURANCE AND INDEMNIFICATION (intro)
nodes.summary: The Consultant must maintain insurance throughout the Agreement for injury or property-damage claims arising from its work. SBCERA may review coverage and require a meeting to address inadequate protection. Before work begins, the Consultant must provide evidence identifying the Agreement and an insurer statement promising at least 30 days’ notice of material policy changes or termination; SBCERA may request certified policies, which the insurer may provide instead of certificates. Required coverage: commercial general liability naming SBCERA as additional insured and primary, with specified endorsements and limits of $1 million per occurrence/$5 million aggregate; statutory workers’ compensation; errors and omissions at $5 million per occurrence and aggregate; fidelity bond covering theft, fraud, and employee dishonesty at $10 million per occurrence and aggregate; and cyber coverage at $10 million aggregate. Deductibles and self-insured retentions require approval and may be reduced or eliminated for SBCERA or secured by a bond covering losses and related expenses.

nodes.title: 8.1.4 Claims Made Professional Liability Insurance If professional liability coverage is written on a Claims Made form:
nodes.summary: For claims-made professional liability coverage, the retroactive date must be on or before the contract date or start of work. If coverage ends without a replacement claims-made policy with a retroactive date before the contract effective date, the Manager must obtain at least five years of extended reporting coverage; claims-reporting requirements must be submitted to SBCERA for review. Insurers must meet Best’s Financial Class X and Policyholder Rating A− standards or receive SBCERA’s written approval. The Consultant must ensure its general liability policies waive subrogation against SBCERA and its trustees, officers, and employees for covered bodily injury or property damage, and document the waiver on the insurance certificate. If a waiver costs extra, the Consultant may pay the premium or use a qualifying insurer that provides the waiver at no charge.

nodes.title: 8.2. Indemnification
nodes.summary: The Consultant must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless SBCERA and its current, former, and future Board members, officers, employees, and agents against claims, losses, liabilities, damages, and expenses (including attorneys’ fees) connected to the Consultant’s services, including negligence, bad faith, willful misconduct, breach of agreement, or breach of fiduciary duty. If a court determines SBCERA was not entitled to indemnification, SBCERA must reimburse the Consultant’s reasonable defense and indemnification costs. Indemnitees must notify the Consultant in writing within 30 days of receiving notice of a claim and provide relevant papers; notice from any source suffices, and failure to notify affects indemnity only to the extent of actual prejudice. The Consultant may participate in and assume the defense using counsel reasonably acceptable to SBCERA. Separate counsel is required when either party reasonably identifies a conflict. SBCERA Indemnitees may participate in or lead the defense without waiving indemnity, and the Consultant may not settle claims without SBCERA’s consent, which may not be unreasonably withheld.

result.title: ARTICLE 9 RECORDS
result.summary: Consultant must provide SBCERA and its authorized representatives access to Agreement-related records during business hours on reasonable notice, never requiring more than five business days. It must retain records for at least five years from creation or longer if required by law, then give SBCERA 60 days’ notice before disposal. During that period, SBCERA may take possession, and Consultant must reasonably cooperate. Record-access obligations survive termination for five years; disposal notice, possession, and cooperation obligations survive for seven years. Except as required by law or court or regulatory order, Consultant must keep all Agreement-related documents and recorded information confidential, including billing and SBCERA records, with the same confidentiality it provides for other accounts.

result.title: ARTICLE 10 GOVERNMENTAL PROVISIONS
result.summary: The agreement is governed by California law, with lawsuits to be brought in San Bernardino County and the parties consenting to local courts’ jurisdiction. Consultant represents that it is an equal-opportunity employer and must take affirmative action against discrimination in hiring and employment, including recruitment, advancement, termination, compensation, and training. Subject to legal or regulatory restrictions, Consultant must promptly notify SBCERA in writing of known complaints or disciplinary actions by specified securities and governmental regulators involving Consultant or relevant investment professionals who served SBCERA during the prior 24 months. Consultant acts as an independent contractor; its personnel are its employees, and it is responsible for their workers’ compensation. Subcontracting requires prior written approval from SBCERA’s Investment Officer, and Consultant alone is liable for contractor payments. The Senior and Alternate Senior Consultants must file Form 700 after signing and annually by April 1; SBCERA will send annual reminders. Because the agreement was negotiated by sophisticated parties represented by counsel, ambiguities will not be construed against the drafter; it will be interpreted reasonably to fulfill its purpose.

result.title: ARTICLE 11 MISCELLANEOUS
result.summary: Article 11 covers miscellaneous terms: the agreement may be signed in counterparts; CONSULTANT may not assign it or its rights or duties without SBCERA’s prior written consent, which SBCERA may deny at its discretion; headings are for convenience only. SBCERA will provide a written list of authorized representatives and specimen signatures, and CONSULTANT may rely on that list until notified of changes. Notices must be written and are effective upon hand delivery with receipt or four business days after qualifying registered or certified mail; the specified SBCERA and consultant addresses may be changed by written notice. Invalid provisions do not affect others. Waivers must be written and specific; failure to enforce is not a waiver, and remedies are cumulative. The prevailing party in litigation may recover reasonable attorney fees. CONSULTANT will cooperate with SBCERA’s other retained advisers. The agreement and exhibits supersede prior understandings; amendments require a written agreement signed by both parties. The text ends with execution blocks for the consultant and SBCERA, plus SBCERA counsel’s approval as to form and legality.
